title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Ageing workforce and senior workers
sections.summary: By 2030 about one in four citizens will be 65 and above, with seniors making up large shares of land transport and F&B workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In Singapore, by 2030, around one in four citizens, will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our resident old-age support ratio reached an all-time low at 3.8 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As of June 2022, 880,000 or roughly one-third of our resident workforce is 50 years and above, 400,000 are 60 years old and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Seniors comprised 54% share of workers in land transport and supporting services, people doing taxi, private-hire car drivers and bus drivers; and 42% of the Food & Beverage (F&B) services, hawkers or food and drink stall assistants.

sections.label: Senior employment rate
sections.summary: The employment rate of seniors aged 65 and above eased from 31.7% in 2021 to 31.0% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our employment rate of seniors aged 65 and above has eased from 31.7% in 2021 to 31.0% in 2022.

sections.label: Part-time Re-employment Grant
sections.summary: MOM's Part-time Re-employment Grant has helped increase part-time re-employment availability for senior workers, and the Ministry was asked to update on its progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: MOM's Part-time Re-employment Grant (PTRG) has helped to increase the availability of part-time re-employment to senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry update on the progress and achievements of the Grant?

sections.label: Productivity and foreign workforce
sections.summary: Without significant productivity improvement over the next decade, Singapore might have to greatly increase its foreign workforce, which already has around 1.3 million Work Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: If we are unable to improve our productivity significantly over the next decade, we might have no choice but to greatly increase our foreign workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: There are already around 1.3 million foreign Work Pass holders in Singapore today.

sections.label: Foreign manpower framework calibration
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked how it would calibrate its foreign manpower framework within the context of an ageing workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share with the House how it would calibrate its foreign manpower framework within the context of an ageing workforce?

sections.label: New social compact
sections.summary: Singapore must act decisively and swiftly to avoid such a predicament and evolve a new social compact within the context of an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We must act decisively and swiftly to ensure we do not find ourselves in such a predicament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We need to evolve a new social compact within the context of an ageing population.

sections.label: SME growth over decade
sections.summary: As of 27 September 2022, there were more than 290,000 SMEs, following consistent growth in the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: As of 27 September 2022, we have more than 290,000 SMEs following consistent growth in the past decade.

sections.label: Grab drivers' prior experience
sections.summary: Two Grab drivers had 12 years construction experience and 20 years in oil and gas, one certified NACE Level 3.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Chairman, I chatted with two Grab drivers during my rides.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: One was a project manager with 12 years construction experience and the second had 20 years in oil and gas and was also a certified NACE Level 3, a specialised coating inspector certification.

sections.label: PMETs and remote working
sections.summary: 60% of the workforce are PMETs, and remote working means Singaporean PMETs compete against a global workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Chairman, while 60% of our workforce are PMETs and flexible work arrangements (FWAs) or some degree of remote working appear to be the norm for our PMETs in this post-pandemic workplace, remote working is a double-edged sword.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With FWAs or remote working, our Singaporean PMET workforce are no longer competing for jobs only within Singapore but rather, we are competing against a global workforce.

sections.label: Singapore Core and licensed workers
sections.summary: The Minister said growing the Singapore Core in every occupation is unrealistic; around 70% of licensed plumbers are above 50.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister replied to say that it would not be realistic to aim to grow the Singapore Core in every single occupation in view of our finite local workforce, with the ageing cohorts larger than the cohorts that are entering the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Around 70% of the licensed plumbers are above the age of 50.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As of end-June 2022, there were close to 4,000 LEWs, of which less than 1% were foreigners from various nationalities on either S Passes or Employment Passes.

sections.label: Plumbing PWM and career model
sections.summary: Straits Times reported NTUC working on a plumbing PWM and a proposed Career Progression Model for skilled trades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 9 January this year, the Straits Times reported that NTUC was looking to work with the Singapore Plumbing Society to effect a Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for the plumbing sector with the NTUC Secretary-General referring to a person is in his or her mid-40s potentially earning $6,000 to $7,000 in vocational trades such as plumbing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Earlier last month, on 9 February, the same newspaper announced the proposed setting up of the Career Progression Model to support the skilled trades industry, covering occupations such as plumbers and electricians, with a view to better career prospects and salaries.

sections.label: Measures and economic storm
sections.summary: SG United Jobs and Skills, SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, PWM and WIS saved businesses and workers during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the SG United Jobs and Skills, SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) all are key measures that have saved our businesses and our workers during the pandemic years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, we are riding straight into a perfect storm with soaring food and energy prices, high interest rates and rising manpower costs and manpower availability.

sections.label: COMPASS and company size
sections.summary: MOM announced COMPASS at last year's Budget for implementation this year, and asks whether it can differentiate companies by size and job skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOM has announced the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) at last year’s Budget and this will be implemented this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can COMPASS differentiate companies by size and job skills, recognising that micro companies may need a lower Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) and some specialist jobs may not have any Singaporeans trained to take up those roles?

sections.label: Fair Practice workplace legislation
sections.summary: Asks how MOM and Tripartite partners intend to manage implementation of the Fair Practice in the Workplace legislation while maintaining workplace harmony.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does MOM and the Tripartite partners intend to manage the implementation of the Fair Practice in the Workplace legislation and achieve its intended purpose while at the same time ensuring that we maintain workplace harmony and not allow for a litigious culture to take root?

sections.label: Capital returns and real wages
sections.summary: States that while returns to conventional capital rise and land fetches higher rent, the real wage earned by human workers will decline.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The result is that while the return to conventional capital is raised and land fetches higher rent, the real wage earned by human workers will decline.

sections.label: Robots complementary to human effort
sections.summary: States there are robots that perform tasks complementary to human effort and thus augment the productivity of human labour.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, there are robots that perform tasks that make them complementary to human effort and thus to augment the productivity of human labour.

sections.label: Robots in labour-scarce economy
sections.summary: States that in a labour-scarce economy like Singapore, adopting robots can boost the return to capital and spur capital investment.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the labour-scarce economy, like Singapore, the adoption of robots can boost the return to capital and spur capital investment.

sections.label: Challenges for businesses and SMEs
sections.summary: States that inflationary pressures, increased interest rates and manpower shortage across many sectors have made it challenging for many businesses, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, the combination of inflationary pressures, increased interest rates and shortage of manpower across many sectors have made it challenging for many businesses, especially SMEs.

sections.label: Insufficient locals for certain roles
sections.summary: Raising productivity still leaves too few locals for roles Singaporeans do not favour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even as we try to raise productivity, there are just insufficient locals to fill the demand for certain roles, especially the ones not favoured by Singaporeans.

sections.label: Funding support for employers hiring
sections.summary: Employers should hire Singaporeans lacking skills and use MOM funding like CSP and CCPs for training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers should be receptive to Singaporeans who fall short of required skills but make use of the relevant funding support such as the Career Support Programme (CSP) and the Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs) that are provided by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This support scheme allows an employer to received funding support from Government to recruit our resident workforce into their company while going through the relevant training to acquire the new skillsets for the new jobs.

sections.label: Support for mature workers and PMEs
sections.summary: It proposes extending JGI, restoring CSP, a Mid-Life Career Transition programme, and raising the $4,000 salary cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, extend the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) and restore the Career Support Programme (CSP) which was the precursor to the JGI to incentivise and encourage employers to hire mature workers, especially PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, introduce a Mid-Life Career Transition programme involving individualised career coaching, advisory and counselling to provide personalised guidance and support for every mature worker including PMEs, whether they are in or out of employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And third, while I applaud the extension of the Special Employment Credit, can MOM consider raising the current $4,000 salary cap to benefit even more mature PMEs?

sections.label: Nationality workplace discrimination complaints
sections.summary: The report found nationality is the most common workplace discrimination, nearly 60% of TAFEP complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The report noted that the most common form of workplace discrimination is nationality, which accounts for close to 60% of the complaints received by the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

sections.label: Diversity quotas for foreign nationalities
sections.summary: MOM should consider diversity quotas limiting the percentage of a company's workforce from one foreign nationality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MOM should consider imposing diversity quotas, or limits on the total percentage of a company's workforce that may be from a certain foreign nationality.

sections.label: Levy on Employment Pass holders
sections.summary: The PSP has repeatedly urged the Government to introduce a $1,200 monthly levy on Employment Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The PSP has also repeatedly urged the Government to introduce a $1,200 monthly levy on Employment Pass holders.

sections.label: Religious practice and employment decisions
sections.summary: Everyone should be free to practise their religion without hindering others from earning a living, noting Recommendation 10 on religious organisations' employment decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Everyone should be free to practise their religion but this should not hinder anyone else from earning a living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I note that Recommendation 10 in the interim report that religious organisations should be allowed to make employment decisions based on religion and religious requirements for all workers.

sections.label: Sexual orientation as protected category
sections.summary: If Recommendation 10 is adopted, the Government is called on to include sexual orientation as a protected category in the anti-discrimination law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If Recommendation 10 is adopted, then I would like to call on the Government to include sexual orientation as a protected category in the anti-discrimination law.

sections.label: TAFEP Guidelines in new law
sections.summary: The Government has announced its intention to enshrine the TAFEP Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices in a new workplace anti-discrimination law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has announced its intention to enshrine the TAFEP Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices in a new workplace anti-discrimination law.

sections.label: Disability definition and accommodations
sections.summary: The law needs an inclusive definition of disability and should require employers to provide reasonable accommodations to PwD employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, it needs a definition of disability that is inclusive of the entire disability population in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, it should require employers to provide reasonable accommodations to PwD employees.

sections.label: Enforceable legislation and remedies
sections.summary: The legislation must be enforceable in a timely manner and provide remedies and measures to prevent repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, the legislation must be enforceable in a timely manner and provide the necessary remedies and measures to prevent repeat offences.

sections.label: Women union leaders on discrimination
sections.summary: In the latest February sensing with women union leaders, 64% agree that discrimination is prevalent in their workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In our latest February sensing with women union leaders, 64% agree that discrimination is prevalent in their workplaces.

sections.label: Foreign workforce size share
sections.summary: Singapore's foreign workforce is 1.31 million, one-third of the total labour workforce, slightly below the pre-COVID-19 level of 1.43 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our total foreign workforce currently stands at 1.31 million, slightly less than the pre-COVID-19 level of 1.43 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This represents one-third of our total labour workforce, a very significant share.

sections.label: Pass salary and DRC changes
sections.summary: Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries rose in September 2022, construction and process sector DRCs fall in January 2024, and the ONE Pass and M-SEP target top talent and strategic businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The qualifying salary for Employment Passes and S Passes has been raised in September 2022 and the reduction of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) for the construction and process sectors will follow suit in January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Overseas Networks & Expertise (ONE) Pass targets the top talents across sectors while the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities (M-SEP) scheme support growth of businesses that contribute to Singapore's strategic economic priorities.

sections.label: M-SEP eligible firms count
sections.summary: Only about 1,000 firms, under 1% of all companies, are eligible for M-SEP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Only about 1,000 firms are eligible for M-SEP or less than 1% of the total number of companies.

sections.label: CPF retirement sum and interest rates
sections.summary: The CPF minimum retirement sum should buffer against unexpected events like price increases, and asks whether CPF interest rates will be revised after 2023 market rates crossed 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, the CPF minimum retirement sum should build in enough buffer for future unexpected events, such as dramatic price increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, as market interest rates crossed 4% in 2023, do we intend to revise the interest rates on the respective CPF Accounts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The CPF LIFE Escalating Plan, which increases payouts by 2% annually, may need to be tweaked, given the changed longer-term inflation outlook.

sections.label: CPF contributions and retirement sums
sections.summary: Appeals to Government, Government-linked and Temasek-linked companies to keep their 17% CPF contribution when workers reach 55, and asks how many Singaporeans reached the Basic, Full and Enhanced Retirement Sums as of December 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
sentences.text: At this juncture, I would like to appeal to our Government, Government-linked companies or even Temasek-linked companies, that are doing well to continue with their 17% contribution instead of reducing it when their workers reach the age of 55 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share as of December 2022, how many Singaporeans have reached the respective Basic, Full and Enhanced Retirement Sums?

sections.label: OCBC and DBS CPF offers
sections.summary: OCBC offers eight-month deposits at 3.88% interest, and DBS accepts online T-bill applications using CPF OA funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: OCBC is now offering eight-month deposits at an interest rate of 3.88%, while DBS now accepts online applications for T-bill investments using CPF OA funds.

sections.label: Government scheme evaluation conclusion
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng said the Government is still evaluating the scheme, and the speaker asks if a conclusion has been reached since August 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Minister Tan See Leng assured us that the Government is still evaluating the scheme and I would like to once again check in if there has been any conclusion on their studies since then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is, after all, close to seven years since August 2016 when the plans were first announced.

sections.label: CPF monies and GIC returns
sections.summary: CPF monies are invested in Special Singapore Government Securities fully guaranteed by the Government, while GIC's portfolio beat inflation at 7.0% nominal and 4.2% real returns over 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While our CPF monies are invested in Special Singapore Government Securities (SGS) fully guaranteed by the Government, GIC's portfolio has been able to beat inflation both nominally and in real terms at 7.0% and 4.2% returns respectively over the past 20 years.

sections.label: CPF Board bank interest rates
sections.summary: The CPF Board assessed major local banks' interest rates at 0.52% from November 2022 to January 2023, which the speaker feels are unrealistically suppressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite this, the CPF Board's assessment of major local banks interest rates to be at 0.52% for the period from November 2022 to January 2023 and one cannot help but feel as though these are unrealistically suppressed, given the realities of the deposit environment of the local banks today.

sections.label: Workplace fatalities and major injuries
sections.summary: MOM said 2022 saw workplace fatalities largely from basic safety lapses, and the annualised major injury rate rose from 16.8 to 18.7 per 100,000 workers in the HSP's first three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM)'s press release stated that "2022 saw a spate of workplace fatalities largely due to basic safety lapses, such as inadequate safety planning and control measures, and non-compliance with safety measures." I also know that the Heightened Safety Period (HSP) which was to have been from September 2022 to February 2023, was extended by three months until 31 May.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: While the workplace fatality rate has improved, unfortunately, the annualised rate of major injuries actually increased from 16.8 to 18.7 per 100,000 workers during the first three months of the HSP.

sections.label: Workplace safety measures and penalties
sections.summary: The speaker asks how many workplace accidents in the past 18 months were due to inadequate management safety measures and whether MOM will make HSP requirements permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: How many of the workplace accidents reported in the past 18 months were due to a lack of or grossly inadequate safety measures by the companies' management?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The recent extension of the HSP notwithstanding, is MOM prepared to make HSP a permanent fixture or at least make permanent some of the HSP requirements, such as the enhanced penalties for systemic WSH lapses?

sections.label: SMEs and WSH outcomes
sections.summary: MOM's data shows that SMEs have the greatest risk of poor workplace safety and health outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM's data also shows that SMEs have the greatest risk of poor WSH outcomes.

sections.label: Graduate starting pay gaps
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong said median starting pay for university graduates is double that of ITE graduates and 1.5 times polytechnic graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong shared in his recent speech at the IPS Singapore Perspectives that today, the median starting pay for a university graduate is double that of an ITE graduate, and 1.5 times that of a polytechnic graduate.

sections.label: NTUC Career Progression Model
sections.summary: The Career Progression Model is cited as uplifting skilled essential tradesmen, and MOM is proposed to survey and publish salaries by skill level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Career Progression Model proposed by NTUC is a good example of uplifting the work prospects and salaries of skilled essential tradesmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Such national-level efforts can ensure that essential skills are continuously and increasingly recognised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I would also propose for MOM to have regular surveying of salaries of specific skills level published, much like how universities publish graduate employment survey and the average salary level for specific graduate course degrees.

sections.label: HR industry transformation map proposal
sections.summary: Targeted foreign worker policies add complexity to HR managers' roles, so an ITM for the HR industry is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Likewise, with MOM’s more targeted foreign worker policies, this creates additional complexities to the role of a HR manager.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose for MOM to introduce an Industry Transformation Map (ITM) for the HR industry and support our HR professionals’ expanded roles which can make a significant improvement in recruitment and valuing skills.

sections.label: Mandating IHRP-certified HR professionals
sections.summary: It is proposed that companies must have at least one IHRP-certified HR professional before hiring foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: First, it would be to mandate companies to have at least one Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP)-certified HR professional before they can be allowed to hire any foreign manpower.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model coverage
sections.summary: The PWM now covers 174,000 lower-wage workers in seven sectors, including food services starting today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: The PWM now covers 174,000 lower-wage workers in seven sectors including cleaning, security, retail and, starting today, the food services industries.

sections.label: Workplace deaths in 2016
sections.summary: Last year saw 46 workplace deaths, the highest since 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, last year saw 46 workplace deaths, the highest since 2016.

sections.label: Migrant workers speaking up
sections.summary: Workers may not speak up for fear of repatriation, so job transfers without employer consent in two scenarios are suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: This can be held against them and they might not dare to speak up for fear of repatriation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: We need to make the playing field less uneven perhaps by allowing workers to transfer jobs without their employers’ consent in two scenarios.

sections.label: WICA claims by designated insurers
sections.summary: Under the Work Injury Compensation Act, designated insurers process all WICA claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Next, under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA), designated insurers process all WICA claims.

sections.label: Cooking facilities in dormitories
sections.summary: It is suggested that every new dormitory be equipped with cooking facilities for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Lastly, on the subject of good quality food for migrant workers, there have been issues in the past and I have spoken on this topic in the House before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I suggest that: one, every new dormitory should be equipped with cooking facilities for workers.

sections.label: CPF contributions for platform workers
sections.summary: Questions are asked on phasing employee CPF contributions and whether opting out stops platform owner contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have several questions pertaining to CPF contributions for platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has been announced that transitional assistance will be provided to platform workers who earn below $2,500 to help them cope with the new requirement to contribute CPF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will MOM be implementing the employee contribution in phases to give them more time to adjust?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If a platform worker opts out, does this mean the platform owner will not need to contribute CPF as well?

sections.label: Discrimination against opt-in workers
sections.summary: It asks whether measures will be put in place to prevent discrimination against those who opt in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will there be measures put in place to prevent discrimination against those who opt in?

sections.label: Update on transitional support
sections.summary: It asks whether the Ministry can provide an update on the transitional support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the transitional support?

sections.label: CPF for low-wage senior workers
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry will help senior workers in low-wage and casual jobs with insufficient CPF, and how companies will retain senior workers despite higher CPF contribution rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: First, it is worrying to learn that certain segments of the population such as senior workers in low-wage and casual jobs do not have sufficient CPF to address their retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: How will the Ministry help this group of people separately?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Separately, notwithstanding the CPF Transition Offset which is for one year, how do we ensure that companies continue to retain their senior workers, given the increase in the senior worker CPF contribution rates?

sections.label: Seniors' retirement adequacy measures
sections.summary: Asks MOM for an update on measures to protect seniors' vulnerability and strengthen their retirement adequacy amid inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: Given the importance of retirement adequacy, especially in inflationary environment, can MOM provide an update on measures that will be put in place to protect the vulnerability of the seniors and strengthen their retirement adequacy?

sections.label: Parent care leave for all workers
sections.summary: States that public servants have had parent care leave for over 10 years and calls for expanding it to all workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: All public servants have had parent care leave for over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time to expand this to all workers.

sections.label: Four-day week and flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Cites a WFH productivity study and UK four-day week findings, notes the White Paper on Women's Development proposal for FWAs, and calls for the 2024 Tripartite Guidelines to be legislated and enforced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: One of many studies has shown that a Chinese company saw a 13% increase in productivity for employees allowed to work remotely in a work-from-home (WFH) experiment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Last year, I called for the public service to take a leadership role and undertake a four-day work week pilot, similar to the one which companies in the UK embarked on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I am pleased to update this House that more than nine out of 10 companies that adopted a four-day working week in the UK trial will continue to use the more flexible way of operating, according to findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: The White Paper on Women’s Development has also proposed Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) to be a "pervasive and sustainable workplace norm", to foster a more inclusive work environment especially for married women who may otherwise leave the workforce significantly earlier than men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: A normalised FWA will enable employees’ FWA requests to be considered fairly, instead of not giving them the real option to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: We understand that there is the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements that will be ready by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: And leading up to this, I find it pertinent to maintain that these guidelines should be legislated and enforced, and not be seen as mere guidelines that leaves companies the option of not even extending this option to their employees.

sections.label: Forms and benefits of FWAs
sections.summary: States that FWAs can be flexi-time, flexi-place and flexi-load, and together with job redesign can unlock employment opportunities for seniors, PwDs, part-time workers and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) can take the form of flexi-time, flexi-place and flexi-load.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: FWAs, together with job redesign, can unlock employment opportunities for seniors, persons with disabilities (PwDs), part-time workers and caregivers.

sections.label: Measure of success for employment schemes
sections.summary: Asks what the measure of success is for the extended Senior Employment Credit, Part-time Employment Grant and new Uplifting Employment Credit for ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: With the extension of the Senior Employment Credit, Part-time Employment Grant and introducing Uplifting Employment Credit for ex-offenders, what is the measure of success for these schemes?

sections.label: Remote work, FWAs, disabled employment
sections.summary: Asks about remote working percentages, especially SMEs, progress of Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements, and notes 65.7% of working-age PwDs are outside the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have any indicators of the percentage of businesses practising remote working, especially for SMEs as there are many friction points in FWAs between employer and employee, such as working hours, hours of working week and performance assessment, just to name.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: What is the progress of the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements and other elements that can be implemented earlier?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Data from the Comprehensive Labour Force Survey (CLFS) released earlier this month on 10 February, showed that among resident Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in the working ages of 15 to 65 in 2021 and 2022, a majority of 65.7% are outside of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given the Ministry of Social and Family Development's (MSF) 2020 estimate of 32,000 PwDs who are of working age, this means about 21,000 working-age PwDs are still outside of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Of those outside of the labour force, a majority of 77% or 16,000 PwDs indicate that they are in poor health, too old or disabled to work.

sections.label: Employment rate of disabled
sections.summary: States that 31.4% of working aged Persons with Disabilities in Singapore are employed as of published statistics earlier this month.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Just 31.4% of working aged PwDs in Singapore are employed as of published statistics earlier this month.

sections.label: Caregivers' high treatment costs
sections.summary: Recalls a Budget speech on high expenses faced by caregivers of people with severe disabilities or rare disorders, with treatment costs up to $200,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In my Budget speech, I had expounded on the high expenses this group of caregivers of people with severe disabilities or rare disorders face, due to the extremely high cost of treatment for their wards, which can amount up to $200,000 a year.

sections.label: Suggestions to help ex-offenders
sections.summary: Notes employers hiring ex-offenders and inmates' fears, and offers three suggestions: incentivise employers and internships, provide career coaching, and support employability skills training with YRSG and SPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As much as it was happy to hear some employers leaning forward to help and hire ex-offenders, we hear the fears and anxieties from the inmates who are soon to be released and want to re-integrate back into society and the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I have three suggestions for MOM to consider to help this group of workers: first, MOM should support and better incentivise and encourage employers, businesses and trade associations to hire ex-offenders as well as offer internship opportunities for them, to assist them to assimilate into these jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, MOM and our career placement agencies, including the private ones, can provide career coaching, advisory and mentoring services for this group of jobseekers, so that we can minimise the expectation mismatch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, MOM working closely with YRSG and SPS can support employability skills training, including job readiness programmes, such as resume and cover letter writing, navigating the job search and job application process before their eventual release.

sections.label: After-hours work communication policy
sections.summary: Asks MOM to provide an update on adoption of after-hours work communication policy by companies based in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Can MOM provide an update on the adoption of such after-hours work communication policy by companies based in Singapore?

sections.label: Studying trends for localisation
sections.summary: Asks whether MOM can study trends and potentially localise legislative and non-legislative ideas for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Can MOM study some of these trends and how we could potentially localise some of these legislative and non-legislative ideas for Singapore?

sections.label: Total employment growth 2022
sections.summary: Total employment grew by more than 200,000 in 2022, surpassing pre-pandemic levels by 3%, with resident employment 4.4% above 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Total employment grew by more than 200,000 in 2022, surpassing its pre-pandemic level by 3%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Resident employment is already 4.4% above 2019 levels.

sections.label: Median income growth residents
sections.summary: Nominal median income of full-time employed residents grew 8.3% in 2021, and real median income growth in 2022 was more than double that of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The nominal median income of full-time employed residents grew by 8.3% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is more than double that of the previous year of 3.2% and even after adjusting for inflation, the real median income growth in 2022 was more than double that of 2021.

sections.label: Tech@SG local jobs created
sections.summary: The Tech@SG pilot created more than 1,500 local jobs in tech startups in the past three years since launch.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Tech@SG pilot has also created more than 1,500 local jobs in tech startups in the past three years since launch.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills placements
sections.summary: From April 2020 to April 2022, around 200,000 locals were placed under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, with 150,000 into permanent jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: From April 2020 to April 2022, the combined efforts of the Government, the unions and the employers supported the placement of around 200,000 locals under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, out of which around 150,000 were placed into permanent jobs, with the rest placed into traineeships and attachment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: WSG and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute's 24 SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres across the country were also able to assist and place 3,400 jobseekers in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Mr Abdul Samad would be happy to know that through customised efforts targeted at key sectors, we helped place more than 11,000 locals into new jobs in these sectors.

sections.label: CCP support mature workers
sections.summary: CCPs provide 90% of salary and training costs for mature workers aged 40 and above; in 2022, WSG supported about 1,900 workers through CCPs and 1,100 through SGUP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I appreciate that mature workers may find it slightly more challenging to switch careers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, the CCPs provide an even higher level of support – 90% of salary and training costs – for mature workers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In 2022, WSG supported about 1,900 workers through CCPs and another 1,100 through SGUP.

sections.label: Job Transformation Maps progress
sections.summary: 10 JTMs have been completed with eight in progress; the Food Manufacturing JTM identified emerging roles and pathways to redesign jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To date, 10 JTMs have been completed, with eight additional JTMs in progress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: One example is the Food Manufacturing JTM launched by Enterprise Singapore in December 2022, which identified emerging job roles such as novel foods technical manager, and set out pathways to redesign jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Workers can reskill themselves via programmes such as the CCP for Food Manufacturing Professionals and Associates and SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes to move into emerging or redesigned roles.

sections.label: CareersFinder job training integration
sections.summary: CareersFinder is the first step to try and integrate job and training recommenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: CareersFinder is the first step to try and integrate job and training recommenders.

sections.label: Redesigning skilled trades with NTUC
sections.summary: NTUC partnership will look into redesigning skilled trades to offer better salaries, career and skill progression ladders, and ways to attract, retain and reward workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But "hands-on" work – the craft required to make something well, to fix a complex machine – is just as important for our society to function, as Mr Edward Chia and Mr Pritam Singh have also highlighted Many of these "hands-on" jobs require deep skills too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are partnering NTUC to look into how we can redesign skilled trades, particularly those that remain indispensable in our future economy, to offer better salaries, clearer career and skill progression ladders and other ways to attract, retain and reward workers in these jobs.

sections.label: Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass
sections.summary: The ONE Pass was announced last year for talent earning at least $30,000 in fixed monthly salary or with outstanding achievements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Last year, I announced the Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) for talent earning at least $30,000 in fixed monthly salary, which comparable to the top 5% of EP holders, or those with outstanding achievements in arts and culture, sports, research and academia.

sections.label: EP, S Pass and COMPASS changes
sections.summary: There will be no change to the EP qualifying salary, but S Pass qualifying salary and Tier 1 levy will increase in September 2023, and COMPASS will apply to new EP applications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This year, there will be no change to the EP qualifying salary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will, however, proceed with the second step of the increase to the S Pass qualifying salary and Tier 1 levy in September 2023, as I had announced last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The S Pass minimum qualifying salary will be raised from $3,000 to $3,150.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The S Pass Tier 1 levy will also increase from the current $450 to $550 in September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: COMPASS – a new, transparent and holistic assessment framework for EP applicants – will be applied to new EP applications from September this year.

sections.label: Shortage Occupation List review
sections.summary: The SOL will include specialised roles in areas such as tech, healthcare and sustainability, and will be reviewed regularly with a major refresh every three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The SOL will include specialised roles spanning areas such as tech, healthcare and sustainability, where there are global shortages of skilled professionals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The SOL will be reviewed regularly, with a major refresh every three years.

sections.label: Bonus criteria details release
sections.summary: Full details on the bonus criteria will be released on MOM's website by the end of March.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Full details on the bonus criteria will be released on MOM’s website by the end of March.

sections.label: NTS Occupation List implementation
sections.summary: The NTS Occupation List starts 1 September, with employers hiring NTS Work Permit Holders subject to an 8% sub-quota and a $2,000 monthly salary criterion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This NTS Occupation List is intended to help firms adjust to the S Pass qualifying salary and levy increases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will hence implement the NTS Occupation List on 1 September this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Employers who wish to hire NTS Work Permit Holders will be subject to a sub-quota of 8% and a fixed monthly salary criterion of at least $2,000.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement enhancements
sections.summary: Enhancements to the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme raise maximum annual payments from $4,000 to $4,200 and expand coverage to over half a million lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We also provide additional support for our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have implemented enhancements to the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS) this year to increase the maximum annual payments, up from $4,000 to $4,200 and expanded the coverage so that over half a million lower-wage workers can benefit.

sections.label: Special Account interest rate
sections.summary: The Special Account interest rate is pegged to the 12-month average yield of 10-year Singapore Government Securities plus 1% and reviewed quarterly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Special Account (SA) interest rate is pegged to the 12-month average yield of 10-year Singapore Government Securities (SGS) plus 1% and is reviewed quarterly.

sections.label: Extra interest on CPF balances
sections.summary: The Government has paid and will continue paying 1% extra interest on the first $60,000 of members' combined CPF balances, including the first $20,000 in OA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On top of this, the Government has and will continue to pay 1% of extra interest on the first $60,000 of members' combined CPF balances, including the first $20,000 in members' OA.

sections.label: CPF monthly salary ceiling increase
sections.summary: The CPF monthly salary ceiling will be raised from $6,000 to $8,000 in 2026 to keep pace with rising salaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To help middle-income Singaporeans save more for retirement, we will also be raising the CPF monthly salary ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000 in 2026 to keep pace with rising salaries.

sections.label: Additional CPF balances and payouts
sections.summary: Raising the monthly salary ceiling for his CPF contributions means he can expect around $100,000 more in combined CPF balances or a $500 increase in monthly CPF LIFE payouts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As a result of just raising the monthly salary ceiling for his CPF contributions, he can expect around an additional $100,000 in his combined CPF balances or a $500 increase in his monthly CPF LIFE payouts if he works until age 65 and starts his payouts then.

sections.label: Annual salary ceiling unchanged
sections.summary: The annual salary ceiling remains unchanged and will limit the impact on business costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The annual salary ceiling, which remains unchanged at this juncture, will also limit the impact on business costs.

sections.label: Reviewing CPF retirement solutions
sections.summary: The government will review solutions within and outside the CPF system to help workers meet basic retirement needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With this in mind, we will review our range of solutions both from within and outside the CPF system, such as work-based incentives and the Silver Support scheme, to give them greater assurance that they can meet their basic retirement needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Ultimately, we want to strengthen our support such that as long as you work, as long as you contribute consistently to your CPF, you will be able to meet your basic retirement needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will provide further updates on our efforts to strengthen the CPF system in due course.

sections.label: Empowering workers and upskilling
sections.summary: Workers will be empowered to find opportunities and helped to upskill, reskill and search for jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In your working years, we will empower you to find and work towards new opportunities if you take the first step.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will also help you to upskill, to reskill and to facilitate your job search based on your skills and interests.

sections.label: Progressive Wages for lower-wage workers
sections.summary: The tripartite Progressive Wages journey began in 2012, and lower-wage workers' real incomes grew 4.7% last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Chairman, our tripartite journey to uplift lower-wage workers through Progressive Wages started more than 10 years ago with the first Progressive Wage Model (PWM) in the cleaning sector in 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Last year, real incomes of lower-wage workers grew by 4.7%, faster than the median worker at 2.0%.

sections.label: 2023 lower-wage worker milestone
sections.summary: All recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers will be fully implemented by July 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The year 2023 is a milestone year in our journey of uplifting lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will see all recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers fully implemented by July.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This follows the implementation of various PWMs, the Local Qualifying Salary requirement and Progressive Wage Mark – last September, and in March this year.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary requirement
sections.summary: The new Local Qualifying Salary requirement was implemented last September for firms employing foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Last September, we implemented the new Local Qualifying Salary (LQS) requirement for all firms that employ foreign workers to pay their local workers at least the LQS.

sections.label: Progressive Wage moves coverage
sections.summary: Food Services PWM and Occupational Progressive Wages for Administrators and Drivers take effect, with Waste Management PWM from July, benefiting up to nine in 10 lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The Food Services PWM and Occupational Progressive Wages for Administrators and Drivers will come into effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With the implementation of the Waste Management PWM this July, the suite of Progressive Wage moves will benefit up to nine in 10 of our full-time lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Workers covered by Sectoral Progressive Wages will see cumulative wage increases of up to 80% or more, by 2028.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Mark companies
sections.summary: About 2,000 companies have received the Progressive Wage Mark since applications opened last December.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since applications opened last December, about 2,000 companies have received the Progressive Wage Mark.

sections.label: WSS eligibility enhancements
sections.summary: WSS eligibility age drops from 35 to 30 and income cap rises from $2,300 to $2,500, making 70,000 more lower-wage workers eligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To allow more lower-wage workers to benefit from WSS and upskill earlier in their careers, we will first lower the eligibility age for WSS from 35 to 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Additionally, workers earning up to $2,500 a month will now be able to qualify for WSS, up from the current qualifying income cap of $2,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With these enhancements, 70,000 more lower-wage workers will be eligible for WSS.

sections.label: Payments to lower-wage workers
sections.summary: Over half a million lower-wage workers will benefit from payments amounting to $1.1 billion, up from $850 million previously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With these enhancements, over half a million lower-wage workers will benefit from payments amounting to $1.1 billion, up from $850 million previously.

sections.label: HSP extension by MOM
sections.summary: From today, MOM has extended the HSP by three months until 31 May 2023 to drive further WSH improvement and maintain vigilance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With effect from today, MOM has extended the HSP by three months till 31 May 2023 to drive further WSH improvement and maintain vigilance.

sections.label: WSH penalties and whistle-blowing campaign
sections.summary: CEOs or boards of companies with serious WSH lapses must attend mandatory WSH training, maximum fines increase, and a whistle-blowing awareness campaign launches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: CEOs or board of directors of companies found to have serious WSH lapses following serious workplace incidents have to attend a mandatory half-day in-person WSH training course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MOM will also increase the maximum fines to deter errant workplace safety and health behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To strengthen the workplace safety and health ecosystem, we will also launch a campaign to encourage and empower workers to speak up on workplace safety and health concerns and raise awareness on the protections for workers who whistle-blow.

sections.label: Workplace safety and health reforms
sections.summary: The Multi-Agency Workplace Safety Taskforce is considering deeper broad-based and sectoral reforms to strengthen workplace safety and health standards sustainably for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: What we do need to do is to strengthen workplace safety and health standards and practices in a sustainable manner for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This is why we are considering deeper reforms, both broad-based and sectoral measures, as part of the Multi-Agency Workplace Safety Taskforce.

sections.label: IHRP-certified professionals growth
sections.summary: The community of IHRP-certified professionals has tripled since 2020 and now numbers over 6,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The community of IHRP-certified professionals has tripled since 2020 and is now over 6,500 strong.

sections.label: HR Industry Transformation Plan
sections.summary: MOM will launch a five-year HR Industry Transformation Plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To this end, Mr Edward Chia will be pleased to know that MOM will be launching a five-year HR Industry Transformation Plan.

sections.label: Progressive Wage coverage expansion
sections.summary: By July this year, Progressive Wage measures will be expanded to cover up to nine in 10 lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: By July this year, we will expand the Progressive Wage measures to cover up to nine in 10 lower-wage workers.

sections.label: Sectoral Progressive Wages wage increases
sections.summary: Workers covered by Sectoral Progressive Wages will see cumulative wage increases of up to 80% or more by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With this, workers covered by the Sectoral Progressive Wages will see cumulative wage increases of up to 80% or more by 2028.

sections.label: Platform workers CPF and compensation
sections.summary: The Government accepted the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers' recommendations in full, with CPF contributions, enhanced representation and work injury compensation starting from the second half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Unlike typical SEPs, platform workers are subject to management control by platform companies and tend to have modest incomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This is why in November last year, the Government accepted the recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers in full.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: CPF contributions to Special and Ordinary Accounts, enhanced representation and also work injury compensation for platform workers will commence from the second half of 2024.

sections.label: CPF alignment for Platform Workers
sections.summary: The Committee recommended aligning Platform Companies' and Platform Workers' CPF contribution rates with employers and employees, phased in from the second half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, unlike employees, Platform Workers only make MediSave contributions on their own and do not receive CPF contributions from the Platform Companies today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Hence, the Committee recommended aligning CPF contribution rates by Platform Companies and Platform Workers with that of employers and employees respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It also ensures a level playing field for all companies operating in the same field in Singapore and allows Platform Workers to receive similar basic protections as employees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This alignment will be gradually phased in, starting from the second half of 2024.

sections.label: CPF for workers above 65
sections.summary: With additional CPF contributions from Platform Companies, Platform Workers aged above 65 receive the same CPF contributions as employees of the same age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In fact, with the additional CPF contributions from Platform Companies, Platform Workers aged above 65 will be able to receive the same level of CPF contributions as employees of the same age, without having to make additional CPF contributions themselves.

sections.label: Phasing in CPF contributions
sections.summary: The Government intends to phase in additional CPF contributions evenly across five years, about 2.5 percentage points yearly for Platform Workers and 3.5 for Platform Companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Ms Hazel Poa will be happy to note that the Government intends to phase in the additional CPF contributions evenly across five years, at around 2.5 percentage points per year for the Platform Workers and about 3.5 percentage points per year for Platform Companies.

sections.label: Offsetting first-year CPF contributions
sections.summary: In the first year, 75% of the additional contribution the Platform Worker makes to the Ordinary and Special Accounts will be offset.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the first year, we will offset 75% of the additional contribution the Platform Worker makes to the Ordinary and Special Accounts.

sections.label: Workfare payments for Platform Workers
sections.summary: Once CPF rates are fully aligned, Workfare payments for Platform Workers will permanently increase to match employees, up to $4,200 yearly with 40% in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Once the CPF contribution rates of Platform Workers have been fully aligned with that of employees, we will also permanently increase Workfare payments for these Platform Workers to match those of employees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This means that eligible Platform Workers could receive up to $4,200 per year, an increase from $2,800 per year today, with 40% of these given in cash compared to the 10% today.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on representation
sections.summary: A Tripartite Workgroup is discussing how a representative body can formally seek mandate to represent Platform Workers collectively through a law-backed framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: A Tripartite Workgroup (TWG), comprising our tripartite partners, representatives from the Platform Companies and also existing Platform Worker associations, is currently in discussions to determine how a representative body can formally seek mandate to represent Platform Workers collectively, through a framework that is backed by law.

sections.label: Tripartite platform work principles
sections.summary: Discussions progress with tripartite partners guided by upholding tripartism and adapting representation for the platform sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The discussions are making good progress and the tripartite partners have been guided by three key principles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: First, stakeholders agree to uphold the spirit of tripartism, which has achieved good outcomes for businesses and workers, and can also help the platform sector evolve sustainably, to benefit both Platform Companies and Platform Workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Second, stakeholders recognise that while the current representation framework in the employment space works well and is a useful reference, the platform space is different from regular employment and the representation model will need to be adapted accordingly.

sections.label: Senior employment rate rise
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2022, employment rates rose for seniors aged 55 to 64 and 65 to 69.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2022, the employment rate rose from 67.6% to 70.6% for seniors aged 55 to 64 and from 44.6% to 47.5% for seniors aged 65 to 69.

sections.label: Support for senior workers
sections.summary: Retirement and re-employment ages were raised to 63 and 68, and the Senior Employment Credit extended until 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen support for our senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We have raised the statutory retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 respectively this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This supports senior workers to continue working longer, if they wish to.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will also extend the Senior Employment Credit (SEC) until 2025 to support employers who hire senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Under the SEC, employers that hire Singaporean workers aged 60 and above and earning up to $4,000 per month can expect up to 8% of wage offsets.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates for seniors
sections.summary: CPF contribution rates for senior workers are being raised, completing the scheduled increase for ages 65 to 70.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong has announced at the Budget, we are committed to raising the CPF contribution rates for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We have implemented the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers' (TWG-OW) recommendation to increase senior workers' CPF contribution rates in 2022 and 2023 and will continue to do so in 2024 to strengthen their retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With this, we will have completed the scheduled increase in CPF contribution rates for workers aged 65 to 70.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Mr Abdul Samad would be glad to hear that by the time we complete the full increase around 2030, those aged 55 to 60 will have their CPF contribution rates equalised to that of younger workers.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements uptake
sections.summary: In 2021, over nine in 10 employees worked in firms providing at least one sustained flexible work arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2021, over nine in 10 employees worked in firms that provided at least one form of FWA on a sustained basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This is up from over seven in 10 employees in 2019.

sections.label: Tripartite guidelines on FWAs
sections.summary: Tripartite partners are working to introduce Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs by 2024, requiring fair consideration of requests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As announced previously, the tripartite partners are working closely to formulate and introduce Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The guidelines will require employers to consider requests for flexible work arrangements fairly and properly.

sections.label: Telecommuting and TAFEP complaints
sections.summary: In 2022 over three in 10 employed residents had telecommuted, and TAFEP has received no complaints of unfair treatment relating to telecommuting in two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha would be happy to know that in 2022, over three in 10 of employed residents had telecommuted at some point in the month they were surveyed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: TAFEP has so far not received any complaints of unfair treatment relating to telecommuting over the past two years.

sections.label: Women jobseekers placed by WSG
sections.summary: Over three years, WSG and e2i placed more than 83,000 women jobseekers across their programmes and services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Over the last three years, WSG and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) have placed more than 83,000 women jobseekers across its programmes and services.

sections.label: Women's employment rate growth
sections.summary: Efforts including Yayasan Mendaki and Daughters of Tomorrow contributed to the employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 rising from 73% in 2020 to 76% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: These include Yayasan Mendaki and Daughters of Tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: These collective efforts have contributed to the growth in employment rate for women aged 25 to 64, from 73% in 2020 to 76% in 2022, despite the pandemic.

sections.label: Employment target for PwDs
sections.summary: In the Enabling Masterplan 2030, MSF and MOM set an employment rate target of 40% by 2030 for PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In the recently released Enabling Masterplan 2030, MSF and MOM set an employment rate target of 40% by 2030 for PwDs.

sections.label: Enhanced wage offsets for PwDs
sections.summary: The Government will raise the additional wage offset from 10% to 20% and extend it from six to nine months, giving employers up to $8,400 in the first year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2022, the EEC benefitted more than 10,000 PwDs, including close to 2,000 who had not been in work for at least six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that the Government will enhance the additional wage offset by raising the support level from 10% to 20% and increasing the support duration from six to nine months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Taken together with the permanent wage offset, employers can receive up to 40% wage offsets for the first nine months of employment when hiring a PwD who has not been working for at least six months and 20% wage offsets thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This means up to $8,400 in wage offsets for the first full year of employment.

sections.label: Credit for hiring ex-offenders
sections.summary: Employers will receive the credit for new ex-offenders hired between April 2023 and December 2025, and the scheme will be reviewed thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Employers will receive the credit for new ex-offenders hired between April 2023 and December 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will review the scheme, thereafter, to assess its effectiveness in improving ex-offenders' employment outcomes, such as job retention and wages.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit for PwDs
sections.summary: The Enabling Employment Credit for PwDs is enhanced, giving employers wage offsets of up to 40% for nine months and up to 20% thereafter, up to $8,400 in the first year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Some may need more support, such as Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) and ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will enhance the Enabling Employment Credit for PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Employers who hire PwDs who have not worked for at least six months will receive wage offsets of up to 40% for a duration of nine months and wage offsets of up to 20% thereafter, amounting up to $8,400 in the first year of employment.

sections.label: Corrections to two earlier statements
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies that median income growth of 8.3% was in 2022, not 2021, and that the Silver Support Scheme was enhanced in 2021, not 2011.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, I had said that the nominal median income of full-time employment residents grew by 8.3% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I wish to clarify that this was the growth rate in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Second, I had said that the Silver Support Scheme was enhanced in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I wish to clarify that it was enhanced in 2021.

sections.label: Recommended grounds for discrimination protection
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee recommended the new legislation provide stronger protection against discrimination on grounds of nationality, age, sex, race, religion, disability and mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Tripartite Committee has recommended that the new legislation provide stronger protection against discrimination on the grounds of nationality, age, sex, race, religion, disability and mental health conditions.

sections.label: Share of discrimination complaints
sections.summary: These grounds account for more than 95% of discrimination complaints received by TAFEP and MOM in the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Together they account for more than 95% of discrimination complaints received by Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) and MOM in the past five years.

sections.label: Discretion for religious organisations
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee recommended allowing religious organisations discretion to make employment decisions based on religion and religious requirements, scoped to places of worship and solely religious organisations, without allowing discrimination on other protected characteristics lacking religious basis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As such, given the purpose and character of religious organisations, the Tripartite Committee has recommended allowing religious organisations the discretion to make employment decisions, based on religion and their religious requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It must be emphasised that this discretion given to religious organisations is very carefully scoped.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It will only apply to places of worship and religious organisations with sole religious purpose and function.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It will also not allow them to discriminate based on other protected characteristics, where there is no religious basis to do so.

sections.label: New CareersFinder feature launch
sections.summary: A new CareersFinder feature will be launched on the MyCareersFuture portal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To assist, we will be launching a new CareersFinder feature on the MyCareersFuture portal.

sections.label: Senior worker employment framework
sections.summary: The passage states it is hard to set a hard target for senior employment and instead an enabling framework is being created.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In looking at whether we should set a target for senior worker employment, it is important to realise that every senior worker, every senior in fact, in Singapore has different aspirations in life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Some prefer to take care of their grandchildren, and some may want to do more of things that they had not been able to do when they were younger.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is very hard for us to set a hard target and force everyone to continue in employment against their wishes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: What we are trying to do here then, in response to the Member's second question, which is related, is to create an enabling framework to allow as many senior workers as possible to remain in employment, if that is their aspiration to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
