sentences.text: So, by progressively raising re-employment ages and retirement ages to give them the legal protection to remain in employment should they choose to do, making sure there are fair employment practices and a legal framework to prevent discrimination against ageism.

sections.label: Publishing worker source list
sections.summary: The passage states that publishing the list openly would let source countries understand Singapore's vulnerabilities given its small market.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To clarify, given the small size of our market relative to many of the other bigger countries in terms of their workforce, if we were to publish the list and make it so open, in many of these countries where the workers come from, they will then understand what are some of our vulnerabilities.

sections.label: Shortage Occupation List reviews
sections.summary: The passage states three years is sufficient runway for the Shortage Occupation List, with yearly reviews and possible earlier response.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The three years, we feel, is a sufficient runway for us to address some of this in the Shortage Occupation List (SOL).

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Just to reassure the Member, that between MTI and ourselves and some of the other sector agencies, we will also conduct yearly reviews.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we do not have to go through the full three years but within one year, if certain shortages have become even more acute, we will not hesitate to respond.

sections.label: Singaporean workers job concerns
sections.summary: The passage states job and wage growth is uneven, cites MOM's 47,400 fourth-quarter 2022 job growth being mostly non-residents, and asks about PMEs and PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I usually do not get that from most of the other Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: However, we have to continue to work on improving the situation for Singaporean workers, because while the job situation has kind of improved because of the reopening, job and wage growth is still very uneven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: For example, even MOM admitted that out of the 47,400 jobs growth in the fourth quarter of 2022, most of those were actually from non-residents and there are some complaints from IT graduates that they are unable to find jobs as soon as they want.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister what makes him and the policymakers so certain that the Singaporean PMEs are not disadvantaged although employers do not need to contribute CPF for Employment Pass holders?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Second question, can I ask whether the Minister will consider accelerating the income increase under the PWM so that lower-income workers can get a minimum of $1,800 of monthly take-home pay by 2024?

sections.label: CPF retirement sum attainment
sections.summary: The passage states the proportion of active CPF members attaining the Basic Retirement Sum at age 55 rose from five in 10 to almost seven in 10.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, the proportion of active CPF members attaining their cohort's Basic Retirement Sum at age 55 has improved from about five in 10 to almost seven in 10 today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We expect this number to increase to about eight in 10 in 2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For members who are able to set aside the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) in 2022, about seven in 10 – about 70% – can choose to set aside the Full Retirement Sum.

sections.label: Platform worker discrimination guidelines
sections.summary: The passage states the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices will be clarified further to include discrimination of platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In that sense, to say that it is a singular relationship between an employer and employee, the nature of it is not a like-for-like comparison.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But what we will do is that the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) will be clarified further to include the discrimination of platform workers.

sections.label: Wage growth for cleaners and security
sections.summary: Security wages rise from $2,585 in 2023 to $3,500 by 2028, and cleaning from $1,570 to $2,400, an 84% increase in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If Members look at the wage growth, for example, security – they are at $2,585 in 2023, today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: By the time they hit 2028, it is $3,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Cleaning is $1,570 but by 2028, they will get $2,400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: That is an 84% wage increase in five years.

sections.label: Support for caregivers
sections.summary: The government commits to providing caregivers the necessary support to fulfil both work and caregiving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: All of us here who have parents will agree too.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We are committed to providing caregivers with the necessary support so that they can fulfil both their work as well as caregiving responsibilities.

sections.label: IHRP skills badges awarded
sections.summary: Between 2021 and 2022, the Institute for Human Resource Professionals awarded over 2,400 skills badges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2022, Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) awarded over 2,400 skills badges.

sections.label: Job Transformation Maps and Job Redesign Centre
sections.summary: About 10 JTMs are completed, including one for HR, with eight more planned, and WSG and IHRP are setting up a Job Redesign Centre of Excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, there are about 10 JTMs which have already been completed, including one for HR, and there are eight more being planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In addition, WSG and IHRP are working to set up a Job Redesign Centre of Excellence, which will work with the sector agencies and the trade associations.

sections.label: CPF contribution rate increases and offsets
sections.summary: Employer CPF contribution rate increases are gradual, not exceeding one percentage point a year, with a CPF Transition Offset in 2024 to mitigate business costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, we understand the employers may be concerned about the impact of business costs, as the Member has raised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Therefore, the increase in employer's contribution rates is at a gradual pace, not exceeding one percentage point a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To mitigate the rise in business costs due to the increase in CPF contribution rates in 2024, we will provide the CPF Transition Offset as we said earlier, so that this will help mitigate some of the cost pressures they face.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We also expect business-cost increase arising from the increase in the CPF contribution rate for senior workers to be modest due to the lower percentage-point increase, compared to the previous increase in 2022 and 2023.

sections.label: Wage growth for cleaners and security
sections.summary: Wage growth is 84% for cleaners and 56% for security officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As I had said, look again at the wage growth: 84% for cleaners and 56% for security officers.

sections.label: Hard caps on foreigner hiring
sections.summary: The speaker calls imposing hard caps on the number of foreigners from each nationality a firm can hire very rigid and overly so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Your approach that you talked about, in terms of imposing hard caps on the number of foreigners from each nationality that the firm can hire, I think the approach is very, very rigid, and it is overly so.

sections.label: COMPASS workforce diversity approach
sections.summary: The speaker calls COMPASS a more nuanced approach that incentivises firms to strengthen their local core and workforce diversity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think that is a more nuanced approach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have introduced COMPASS which takes a very nuanced position by incentivising firms to strengthen their local core and their workforce diversity.

sections.label: Levy versus EP talent focus
sections.summary: The speaker says imposing a levy is easy for the Government but at the EP level the focus is differentiating and attracting the highest quality talent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: You keep harping on this thing about imposing a levy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is easy enough for the Government to do so because it generates revenue.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But at the EP level, Mr Leong, our focus is on making sure that we can differentiate, that we can get the best, the highest quality, the highest qualified talent anywhere in the world, to come here.
